prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: مواقيت الصلاة في مدن سعودية (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 6 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "المدينة" · longest unbreakable word 49px · one-line width 91px
  col 2: header "الفجر" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 3: header "الظهر" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 4: header "العصر" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 5: header "المغرب" · longest unbreakable word 47px · one-line width 47px
  col 6: header "العشاء" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 41px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 414px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 413px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A quick-reference timetable of daily prayer times for six Saudi cities: readers look up one city's day, or compare one prayer across cities.","reading":"Right-to-left: the eye lands on the city name (row header) first, then sweeps left across the five prayer times; the dominant comparison is column-wise (same prayer across cities), with row-wise reading as the secondary mode.","groups":["col 1 (المدينة) is the row identifier and must be visually separated from the data block","cols 2–6 (الفجر، الظهر، العصر، المغرب، العشاء) are five instances of the same kind of value — clock times — and should read as one uniform band, with no column appearing more important than another"],"keep_intact":["every time value, e.g. 8:16, 12:24, 3:23 — they must never wrap or break at the colon","the single-word headers الفجر، الظهر، العصر، المغرب، العشاء, which cannot wrap and set each column's minimum width"],"may_wrap":["city names, especially المدينة المنورة (two words) and مكة المكرمة — wrapping them to a second line is harmless because the row height already accommodates two lines"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [73, 68, 68, 68, 68, 68] · table 414×301px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [112, 56, 56, 59, 68, 62] · table 414×255px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [91, 60, 60, 62, 70, 70] · table 414×301px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r0A","good":"The five prayer columns are all 68px, so they read as one uniform band of like values; every time has 47px of content space and never touches a border, and all five headers fit with slack.","problems":"The row identifier is the most cramped element in the table: the header المدينة (49px) sits in 52px of content, nearly touching its borders, and مكة المكرمة / المدينة المنورة break into two lines, pushing rows 2–3 to 60px and destroying the row rhythm a column-wise scan depends on.","cause":"Giving all five time columns the same 68px — the minimum forced by the 47px المغرب header — leaves only 73px for col 1, i.e. 52px of text against a 49px longest word."},{"design":"r0B","good":"Every cell is on one line, all rows are a uniform 36px, the table is 46px shorter than the others, and no header wraps; the widths are content-minimal (35/35/38/47/41 header + 21 padding = exactly 56/56/59/68/62).","problems":"There is no breathing room: the clock values sit flush against the cell borders, and the band is visibly unequal — المغرب at 68px is 12px wider than الفجر and الظهر at 56px, so one prayer column looks more important than the rest.","cause":"Allocating 112px to col 1 (exactly the 91px one-line city width + padding) consumes all the slack, leaving precisely the 301px the five header minimums demand and nothing to distribute."},{"design":"r0C","good":"The 91px city column gives the wrapped compound names room, and the two-line rows are at least consistent (rows 2 and 3 both 60px) so the wrap reads as a decision rather than an accident.","problems":"91px (70px content) is an unhappy middle: too narrow for the 91px one-line city name, far wider than the 49px longest word, so the extra space buys nothing while the time columns go without. The band is also uneven for no content reason (60,60,62,70,70): المغرب and العشاء get 8–10px more than الفجر/الظهر, implying a hierarchy that does not exist.","cause":"The city column was set just past its longest word instead of either exactly at it or at the full one-line width, and the remaining 322px were handed out without reference to the header widths 35/35/38/47/41."}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"even-band","widths":[79,66,66,66,68,68],"change":"Takes 2px from each of الفجر/الظهر/العصر in r0A (66 still clears their 59–62px header minimums) and hands the 6px to the city column, 73→79, giving المدينة 58px of content and its words real slack. The band stays effectively uniform (a 2px step is invisible) while every time keeps 45–47px, and no header is within 2px of wrapping."},{"name":"uniform-air","widths":[72,68,68,68,68,69],"change":"Keeps r0A's perfectly uniform 68px band, sends the single spare pixel to العشاء (the widest header after المغرب), and trims the city column to 72px — still 51px of content against a 49px longest word. Maximum air and rhythm for the time values, minimum but legal room for the city names; the tightest of the uniform-band options."},{"name":"wrap-air","widths":[84,65,65,64,69,66],"change":"Commits openly to two-line city names: a genuinely wide row-header column (63px content) so المدينة المنورة and مكة المكرمة break at the space into balanced halves with air around them, and a band that varies by only 5px (44/44/43/48/45px of content) instead of r0C's arbitrary 8–10px jumps. Trades the 36px row rhythm for a comfortable identifier and comfortable numbers at the same time."}]}
